newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELAN STRIKE HITS STEEL OUTPUT - SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELAN STRIKE HITS STEEL OUTPUT - SOURCE.

text.p: Venezuelan steel production was severly hit by Wednesday's national strike, but aluminium output was maintained by non-unionised staff, sources at the state-owned metals conglomerate CVG said.
A senior official at SIDOR, CVG's iron and steel subsidiary, said 70 percent of workers had obeyed the strike call.
"We are operating at minimum level and our daily production of 6,000 tonnes of steel is paralysed, as are deliveries to other companies," the official said.
A spokesman for the aluminium sector, including the companies Venalum, Alcasa, Bauxilium and Carbonorca, said: "Operations are being maintained succesfully by our contingency plan."
Only 40 percent of aluminium workers obeyed the strike call, the spokesman said, and Venalum's daily production of 1,200 tonnes of aluminium was not affected.
The Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), the country's largest union, called the 12-hour stoppage to protest at the private sector's failure to make promised wage rises.
